title: In Vivo Imaging of Human 11C-Metformin in Peripheral Organs: Dosimetry, Biodistribution, and Kinetic Analyses
authors: Gormsen LC, Sundelin EI, Jensen JB, Vendelbo MH, Jakobsen S, Munk OL, et al.
followUp: dynamic imaging for 90 minutes after intravenous and 120 minutes after oral tracer
population: Nine subjects, three women and six men; whole-body dosimetry and biodistribution in four, tissue kinetics in the remainder
funder: No funding statement appears in the article; the disclosure section states only that page charges were paid and that no potential conflict of interest relevant to the article was reported, so study funding could not be determined.
authorConflicts: No potential conflict of interest relevant to this article was reported.
result: Whole-body positron emission tomography of carbon-11-labelled metformin showed uptake primarily in the kidneys, urinary bladder and liver, and to a lesser extent in salivary glands, skeletal muscle and intestines. Effective doses were 9.5 microsieverts per megabecquerel after intravenous and 18.1 after oral administration. Liver kinetics fitted a reversible two-tissue compartment model with a volume of distribution of 2.45 mL/mL with arterial input and 2.66 mL/mL with portal and arterial input; renal data did not fit compartmental models and the volume of distribution was estimated linearly at 6.83 mL/mL. Skeletal muscle and intestinal kinetics showed only discrete tracer uptake, and only slow accumulation was observed in muscle. Liver uptake was pronounced after oral administration, with a tissue-to-blood ratio double that after intravenous administration. No elimination of the tracer through the bile was observed after either route.
